results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** Countable choice, the knots and oriented Seifert surfaces, and the fixed oriented connected-sum convention. We work first over $R=\mathbb F_2[U]$ with the full disk differential, retaining every positive $z$ multiplicity; localization will give the infinity complex. An ordinary doubly pointed model has one $w$ and one $z$, with generators placed at $(i,j)=(0,A_F(x))$.

[F1] Actual full-marked disk counts, finite polynomial differentials, connected-generator relative indices and relative Alexander gradings are established. Good end paths exclude nonconstant strips of nonpositive index. [[thm-balanced-knot-data-admit-full-marked-square-zero-holomorphic-counts]] [[thm-balanced-s-three-knot-generators-admit-consistent-relative-gradings]]

[F2] Actual strictly admissible polygon counts apply also to intermediate three-manifolds other than $S^3$. They retain all nonnegative marked degrees, and give finite triangle maps, their chain-map equations, coherent perturbations and the required parameter homotopies. These statements do not themselves give a top cycle or the multiplication equivalence constructed below. [[thm-strictly-admissible-triple-free-polygons-have-full-marked-low-dimensional-counts]] [[lem-os-disk-and-polygon-analytic-foundations]]

[F3] The actual constant-root inverse, torus mean inverse and supported dipole responses, and the exhaustive torus-target plumbing calculation are available. We use the displayed responses of ordinary stabilization, not its conclusion for a cancelling $S^3$ handle, and check below the changed two-crossing torus and marked-point transfer. [[lem-transverse-linear-strip-cauchy-riemann-isomorphism]] [[lem-real-boundary-strip-cauchy-riemann-inverse-with-free-end-constants]] [[lem-flat-complex-torus-cauchy-riemann-mean-inverse-and-normalized-dipoles]] [[thm-balanced-knot-ordinary-stabilization-has-full-minus-inverse-maps]]

[F4] Same-handlebody top generators are actual cycles; their top products have count one and no positive marked terms. Full-minus auxiliary and attaching-move maps have finite polynomial filtered inverses and inverse homotopies. [[lem-same-handlebody-model-top-counts-have-no-positive-marked-terms]] [[thm-balanced-knot-full-minus-auxiliary-continuations-are-filtered-equivalences]] [[thm-balanced-knot-attaching-moves-have-full-minus-inverse-maps]] Its actual small-copy operation retains one positive core in each old region, balances exact-copy lunes, and proves the unique nearest thin triangle by a bounded scalar inverse. [[thm-globally-weak-hat-handleslides-have-explicit-inverse-homotopies]], Proof3.1–6.1.

[F5] The polygon relative index identifies actual Spin-c differences, rather than formal domains only. The negative modified Morse field on the knot exterior has the explicit zero-relative-Euler zero-surgery cap. Its normalized Alexander value is half the relative Euler number of its perpendicular plane on the exterior Seifert surface, with boundary section $\partial_\lambda=-\partial_\theta$; the cap contributes zero. The local tube model is $f=\sin t(1-r^2/2)$, its selected generator trajectory modifications are outside that tube, and its value is preserved by followed mark-free attaching isotopies. The normalized full-minus comparisons preserve this absolute origin and the degree-zero total-hat Maslov origin. [[lem-doubly-pointed-knot-morse-fields-have-a-zero-framed-seifert-extension]] [[thm-doubly-pointed-s-three-moves-preserve-the-seifert-normalized-filtration]] [[thm-handle-cancellation]] [[lem-heegaard-polygon-spin-c-difference-is-the-capped-periodic-domain]] [[lem-heegaard-polygon-relative-maslov-variation-is-chern-plus-marks]]

[F6] Finite filtered complexes with one-dimensional total homology have additive tensor threshold. The fixed oriented boundary gluing represents the well-defined oriented connected sum. [[lem-tau-additive-for-filtered-tensor-products]] [[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]] [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]]



1.1 Choose finite doubly pointed good diagrams $(\Sigma_1,\alpha,\beta,w_1,z_1)$ and $(\Sigma_2,\xi,\eta,w_2,z_2)$ and their actual full count data from [F1]. Remove disks at $z_1,w_2$ and join their oriented boundaries; retain $w_1,z_2$. The two knot arcs ending at the removed points concatenate across that cylinder. Their other ends, and the boundary-parallel arc witnesses in both handlebodies, are unchanged. This is the oriented connected-sum neck. For the multiplication triple use the three systems $A=\alpha\cup\xi'$, $B=\beta\cup\xi$, $C=\beta'\cup\eta$, where primes are separately labeled sufficiently small exact Hamiltonian copies. Give each copied circle a Morse function with one maximum and one minimum, chosen away from its finitely many old intersection points. The maximum crossings specify $\Theta_\beta,\Theta_\xi$. In a cut handlebody, carry its complete disk system to meridians of the standard boundary-connected sum of solid tori; this gives an actual split product-circle model for these copied systems. These are diffeomorphisms of the diagram and its arc witnesses, not extra analytic identifications. [F1, F4, F6, given, construct]

1.2 We first establish the required split one-handle inclusion, including a mark moved across its neck. Let $E$ be a flat torus with a circle and a small exact Hamiltonian copy, having top and bottom crossings $c_+,c_-$. Put its plumbing point $a$ and its new mark $b$ off the narrow isotopy annuli and off these crossings. Let $D_1,D_2$ be its two elementary bigons. Lifting boundary paths to the plane identifies the relative class ambiguity with the kernel of $\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z^2$ sending the two circle windings to their common primitive slope; since the torus has zero second homotopy, this kernel is precisely the annular period $P=D_1-D_2$. Its area is zero by exactness and it has both signs. A self-end domain is $kP$; a forward domain is $(k+1)D_1-kD_2$, nonnegative only for $k=0,-1$; a reverse domain has coefficients $k-1,-k$, never both nonnegative. Thus a nonconstant holomorphic self-end strip would have zero area and cannot exist. From $c_+$ to $c_-$ there are exactly the two positive bigons in the isotopy annuli, each a disk with its two corners and hence a unique representative modulo translation by the disk Riemann map; reflection or the transverse strip inverse gives its regularity and count one. Both bigons miss $a,b$. A reverse-direction class has negative area, so cannot occur. The other periodic classes change neither these areas nor the mark vectors. These are the actual split $S^1\times S^2$ top data, not the once-intersecting cancelling torus. [F3, F4, construct, algebra]

2.1 Plumb $E$ at a point $q$ in the region of the old mark to be transferred, and place the transferred mark at $b$. Choose $q$ a regular simple-root value for every old rigid strip, with distinct physical incidence positions; this is possible in a small disk of its old marked region because the finitely many protected holomorphic root maps have finitely many critical and discriminant values there. Moving the mark within that region changes no domain coefficient or represented pointed knot. Use a smaller disk on which the whole incidence tensor is standard. At a self-end limit the principal torus root is the constant $c_+$ by step 1.2. Every old simple incidence at $q$ then contributes one inclusion copy of $E$ with two source punctures, one at $a$ and one at $c_+$. Its local equations are exactly the constant-root equations in [F3]: for residues $\lambda_j=\epsilon L_j$ at positions $b_j$ the transverse strip response is $\sum\chi_j\lambda_j/(z-b_j)-Q_\perp D(\sum\chi_j\lambda_j/(z-b_j))$; the physical projection uses the real/real inverse, retaining its right real end constant. The torus response subtracts its mean using a supported density away from both punctures. Transfer of a positive Laurent mode multiplies it by $(\epsilon/r^2)^n$ or $(\lambda_j/r^2)^n$. The resulting trace equation has operator norm $O(|\epsilon|)$, and its divided mean equations are $A_j+L_j+O_{C^1}(|\epsilon|)=0$, where $A_j\ne0$ is the old simple-root inverse derivative. Thus they have the unique solution $b_j=w_j+O(|\epsilon|)$, $L_j=-A_j+O(|\epsilon|)$. The two transverse boundary lines near $c_+$ may have any fixed nonzero angle: their strip inverse in [F3] applies unchanged. No global straightness of the two copied circles is needed by this response. [F1, F3, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

2.2 **Construct the compatible connected Morse data.** Use [F5]'s actual tube coordinates on each input, with its Seifert collar $\theta=0$ and its function $f=\sin t(1-r^2/2)$. Choose the connecting disks about $z_1,w_2$ so small that their knot-tube neighborhoods miss every selected index-one/index-two generator trajectory tube. The lower and upper pieces of the connected surface bound the boundary-connected sums of the respective handlebodies. Before cancelling their tree handles the lower half has its two old minimum balls and the joining one-handle; the upper half has its two old maximum balls and the joining two-handle. Put the joining handle cores on the concatenated lower and upper bridge arcs. This is possible in the product neighborhoods of their boundary-parallel witness disks: the joining core and the two old bridge pieces are an interval in that product, and the collars of $F_1,F_2$ extend across it as the untwisted connected-sum Seifert ribbon. The lower interval contains, in order, one old minimum, the new index-one point, and the other old minimum. Cancel the first minimum with the joining index-one point; dually cancel the second maximum with the joining index-two point in the upper interval. These are the tree-edge zero/one cancellations (and their reversed two/three versions): one joining-handle foot is on each old ball, hence the attaching zero-sphere meets the cancelled ball's belt sphere once. No old higher-index handle or selected generator trajectory is cancelled. After cancellation there is precisely one minimum and maximum and the two original higher-index systems. Thus the result is actual compatible Morse data for the connected diagram of step1.1, with its concatenated bridge witnesses, not an arbitrarily assigned nonzero exterior field. [F1, F5, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Verify exhaustion and the index, rather than assuming a tensor differential. The root determinant transition is $-\epsilon/\xi^2$ at each target matching; its squared winding is minus four, cancelled by the four additional projection branch orders of the torus dipole. Consequently a self-end reference has the old index. Any additional same-domain ambiguity here is an exact-copy annular period with zero Chern evaluation in the torsion pair sector, so the general relative index formula [F5] gives the same index for each actual class; the comparison is not relying on the new manifold being $S^3$. The extraction in [F3] uses only fixed old-core estimates, bounded nonnegative domain coefficients, Laurent expansion on target annuli, and finite projection branching. Those arguments apply to this same plumbing before identifying its torus principal map: here step 1.2 makes it constant at its specified crossing. The additional torus annular periods have zero area, so cannot add a positive component or an unbounded domain ray. Old boundary disks and closed horizontal degrees have index at least two, exactly as in the referenced determinant calculation. At total index one a self-end limit therefore contains exactly one old rigid strip. Its simple incidences force one degree-one torus per incidence and no branching matching tree. The converse response and residue estimate $\lambda+\epsilon A+o(\max|\lambda|+|\epsilon|)=0$ force every convergent solution into step 2.1's unique response neighborhood. Its normalized kernel is zero by the same trace/mean inverse, so the actual operator is onto. A top-to-bottom limit has the single bigon of step 1.2 and old index zero; the good old path forces its old component to be constant and its incidence list empty. Its two bigons cancel with identical marked vectors. For a bottom self-end the identical constant-root argument applies; a bottom-to-top principal component has negative area by step 1.2 and is impossible. These facts for ALL the split-factor generators also exclude a nonconstant nonpositive-index end path. Finally each degree-one inclusion torus passes through $b$ once, so the NEW $b$ multiplicity equals the OLD $q$ multiplicity, including positive multiplicities. All other marks are untouched. Hence $x\mapsto x\times c_+$ is an actual full-polynomial chain inclusion preserving the transferred and retained mark degrees. This proves the operation for the supplied split factor; no assertion about arbitrary nontrivial summand-neck disk matching has been used. [F1, F3, step 1.2, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

3.2 **Check the cancellation fields and their Seifert frames.** Here are local functions for the preceding cancellations, retaining the surface and knot. Write the relevant interval as $K=\{y=z=0\}$ and its Seifert ribbon as $F=\{z=0,y\ge0\}$. The old minimum tube model is converted to $x^2+y^2+z^2$ by $x=\operatorname{sgn}(t-t_0)\sqrt{1+\sin t}$ and radial rescaling $(y,z)\mapsto\sqrt{-\sin t/2}(y,z)$ near $t_0=3\pi/2$; both changes preserve this ribbon and its normal direction. Use the analogous negative model at a maximum. The joining handle and its paired minimum have the local family $f_s=x^3/3-sx+y^2+z^2$, with the product metric. For $s>0$ its two critical points on the interval have indices one and zero; for $s<0$ there is none. This family can be made fixed on its two end collars: write its longitudinal derivative as $x^2-s\chi(x)$ on a compact inner interval, with $\chi=1$ near the cancelling pair; compensate its changed integral by a bump on an outer collar where the derivative is bounded away from zero. Restrict the parameter interval so that this correction preserves that bound. Integration then keeps both end values fixed and introduces no other longitudinal zero; smooth product collars match the old Morse levels. The transverse quadratic coefficient remains positive, so off the interval the gradient cannot vanish. The upper cancellation uses $-f_s$. On the wider tube use the original normal-even functions and a metric splitting the ribbon tangent plane from its normal line; the product collars agree with these choices. Hence throughout both actual cancellations the negative gradient is tangent to the Seifert ribbon, and its nonzero normal vector is a nowhere-zero section of its perpendicular plane on the EXTERIOR, including where the critical pair has disappeared. Degeneracy at $s=0$ occurs only on $K$, which is excised. After cancellation the restricted function on the knot circle has exactly one minimum and maximum, on its lower and upper bridge respectively. Reparametrize its two monotone intervals to the sine-model intervals, retaining the ordered marks. In the thin tube the longitudinal derivatives then have the same sign away from those extrema, and at an extremum the transverse quadratic signs agree with the sine model. Interpolate the longitudinal derivative and transverse coefficient there to the sine model, keeping the transverse sign fixed near each extremum and the longitudinal derivative nonzero on its complement. The resulting negative gradients have no zero off $K$, remain tangent to the Seifert collar, and keep its normal section. Choose the corresponding product metrics and carry these tube coordinates into the actual compatible Morse data; the zero-relative-Euler filling of [F5] is now precisely its prescribed sine-model filling. All selected trajectory modifications lie outside these supports and are exactly the original modifications. Tiny copied attaching curves follow their mark-free isotopies in [F5], carrying this field comparison to the distinguished product generator. [F5, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

4.1 Iterate step 3.1 over the split meridian factors of step 1.1. Associating their connected sums in sequence and carrying the mark to the last factor gives precisely the original neck and its surviving mark, by their product collar coordinates. This constructs the chain maps $\iota_1(x)=x\times\Theta_\xi$ and $\iota_2(y)=\Theta_\beta\times y$ into the $AB$ and $BC$ complexes. In the first map $z_1$ is transferred to $z_2$; in the second $w_2$ is transferred to $w_1$. Thus the first input's $w$ exponent and the second input's $w$ exponent have the same actual action in the common triple. All additional torus top factors are cycles, and the iterated cancellation of their paired bigons is literal over $\mathbb F_2$. The intermediate manifolds are $S^3\#^{g_2}(S^1\times S^2)$ and $\#^{g_1}(S^1\times S^2)\#S^3$ in their torsion sectors. Their normalized periodic domains are generated by exact-copy annuli and have zero area, hence both signs. For the multiplication triple this lattice identification can be checked integrally: in the first surface a relation has the form $a\alpha+(b+c)\beta=0$, so $a=0,b=-c$ because the $S^3$ meridians give complementary integral sublattices; in the second it is $(a+b)\xi+c\eta=0$, so $a=-b,c=0$. Thus only the two families of exact-copy annuli remain, modulo the outgoing normalized $S^3$ periodic domain, which is zero. A positive area form may therefore be chosen first and the copies made exact for that form; no unsupported claim that arbitrary strong admissibility annihilates periods is needed. Apply the general-manifold sector branch of [F2] to these actual good ends. [F2, F4, step 1.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 Compose these inclusions with the actual weighted triangle map of [F2]. It gives the finite polynomial chain map $\Gamma$ whose infinity notation is $$\Gamma([x,i_1,j_1]\otimes[y,i_2,j_2])=\sum_{v,\ \mu(\psi)=0}\#\mathcal M(\psi)\,[v,i_1+i_2-n_{w_1}(\psi),j_1+j_2-n_{z_2}(\psi)].$$ The inputs of $\psi$ are $x\times\Theta_\xi$ and $\Theta_\beta\times y$. Replacing either input by its $U$ multiple lowers the sum $i_1+i_2$ by one and gives the identical output $U$ multiple, with unchanged triangle class; thus the formula is $R$-balanced. Its chain-map equation is the actual triangle boundary equation, after the two chain inclusions just proved. The full nonnegative $w_1,z_2$ degrees are retained. The generator origins needed to read the displayed $j$ coordinate will be checked by the Seifert-cap calculation below; at this stage the formula is the corresponding relative-filtration formula. [F2, F4, F5, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 Prove the leading coefficient by the actual small-copy operation in [F4], rather than assuming that a top cycle makes it one. In the first surface it is the small-copy triangle at $x$ for $(\alpha,\beta,\beta')$, and in the second the reverse-family small-copy triangle at $y$ for $(\xi',\xi,\eta)$. The operation chooses the copy crossing away from all old crossings, straightens the old opposite arc while preserving the copied-circle model, and gives the unique scalar triangle with bounded inverse and count one. Its root supports are disjoint; the product inverse is therefore the direct sum of those actual inverses. Their domains avoid the neck disks and both surviving marks. They consequently define the same product triangle in the connected target, without any root entering the target neck, and persist under the protected coherent perturbation. To check the other domains use precisely the retained-core construction in that operation: retain a point and a small disk in every old region, and the private positive and negative lune disks of every copy. A triangle confined to the thin copy ribbons must have the nearest output, because each opposite arc in such a ribbon has its single old crossing and the top corner starts its one prescribed partial lune. Its domain and representative are the just proved unique small triangle. Every other nonnegative triangle domain contains one retained old-region core. Balance the private exact-copy lunes and use the positive periodic-annihilating form of step 4.1, with fixed lower area $m_0>0$ on all those cores and unsigned ribbon area $O(\epsilon)$. This bounded-density adjustment is exactly the finite region-bump construction in [F4]: balance each private signed lune, then correct the $O(\epsilon)$ changes of old periodic evaluations in one invertible finite minor off the ribbons. Densities remain positive. The core estimate and the protected small-triangle inverse therefore hold uniformly, and every other contributing triangle has area at least $m_0-O(\epsilon)$ while all nearest areas are $O(\epsilon)$. Take $\epsilon$ so small that this is a strict gap. This is a positive-core/domain argument, not a claim that an arbitrary area-small triangle automatically has count one. The common data in [F2] may be taken sufficiently close to this reference retaining its protected cores, small models and regular ends, as in the actual weighted attaching construction [F4]. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

7.1 **Evaluate the actual absolute origin.** In [F5]'s finite Euler computation, remove the small joining rectangles from the two exterior Seifert surfaces where their tube-normal sections already extend without zeros. This changes neither relative Euler obstruction. Join their remaining surface pieces by step7.2's ribbon. Its normal section agrees with those old sections and with the Seifert boundary section $\partial_\lambda=-\partial_\theta$, up to a constant nonzero real factor. The oriented untwisted gluing makes these factors constant along each seam; they have zero circle winding. Thus the ribbon contributes zero: subdividing the surfaces and ribbon into finitely many framed cells, all internal seam windings cancel and the obstruction is the sum of the two old obstructions. The new longitude is the boundary-connected-sum Seifert longitude. Its explicit zero-relative-Euler cap, as well as each old cap, contributes zero by [F5]. Consequently for the distinguished nearest generator $x'\times y'$ the actual normalized values satisfy $A_{F_1\natural F_2}(x'\times y')=A_{F_1}(x)+A_{F_2}(y)$. This uses actual compatible negative-Morse data from step7.1, with the exterior sections verified in step7.2; it assumes neither that an attaching curve is a physical meridian nor that a closed S3 periodic domain is a zero-surgery Seifert domain. For every other triangle compare its actual trajectory line cochain with this smooth nearest reference, as in [F5]'s absolute attaching-map comparison: cap its attaching-circle terms by their supplied knot-disjoint compression disks. The only uncancelled crossings of its spanning incidence chain with the oriented knot occur positively at $z_2$ and negatively at $w_1$. Its determinant difference is twice their signed count, so its Alexander difference is $n_{w_1}-n_{z_2}$ in the output convention of step5.1. This gives that step's absolute $j$ formula. The distinguished identification and the actual triangle map are therefore bifiltered, with respectively zero losses and the nonnegative marked losses $n_{w_1},n_{z_2}$. The actual boundary sum of the chosen minimum-genus surfaces is the surface used here; no genus-additivity theorem is needed for this Chern evaluation. [F5, step 1.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 2.2, step 3.2, construct, algebra]

8.1 Construct a FINITE polynomial inverse. Identify the outgoing basis with $x\otimes y$ by the distinguished small triangles. Triangle relative index gives a common Maslov shift for this nearest identification and $\Gamma$; temporarily subtract it from the outgoing grading. Every coefficient $U^a v$ is then homogeneous, $M(v)-2a=M(x\otimes y)$, and $a\ge0$. For a ZERO-exponent nonnearest term subtract its distinguished small triangle. Its corrected area is strictly positive by step 6.1. Along any closed walk of such terms the outgoing corner paths glue: the two incoming paths cancel with their small references, leaving an actual normalized periodic domain, not a purported nonnegative difference domain. Its $w$ coefficient is zero. The integral attaching-lattice calculation in step 4.1 identifies its lattice as the exact-copy annuli and the normalized outgoing $S^3$ periods, whose area is zero. Hence a closed walk of zero-exponent terms would have simultaneously positive and zero corrected area. This proves that the zero-exponent coefficient graph has no directed cycle. It requires neither a globally asserted action potential nor a positivity claim for reference-subtracted domains. [F2, F5, step 4.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, construct, algebra]

9.1 Write the actual matrix as $I+N$. On a directed cycle in its finite monomial coefficient graph Maslov homogeneity gives $2\sum a=0$. Since $a\ge0$, every edge of the cycle has exponent zero, contradicting step 8.1. Thus the whole graph is acyclic. A positive-$U$ diagonal term is excluded by its degree, and a zero-exponent diagonal correction by its positive corrected area. If there are $d$ basis generators, $N^d=0$, so $(I+N)^{-1}=I+N+\cdots+N^{d-1}$ is a genuine finite matrix over $R$. It is a two-sided chain inverse because $\Gamma$ is a chain map. Both $N$ and every term in this inverse preserve both filtrations by step 7.1. There is no completion and no inversion of a polynomial such as $1+U$. The outgoing copied diagram already represents the oriented connected sum by step1.1; carry its copies back by the actual mark-free attaching isotopies in [F4] and [F5]. Their finite normalized filtered inverses and homotopies give the equivalence for the chosen connected-sum diagram. Apply [F5] to compare arbitrary normalized input and output models. Tensor the two input comparisons and their inverses over $R$; expanding their finite inverse identities gives tensor inverse homotopies, still bifiltered. Composing these actual equivalences requires no canonical naturality or uniqueness of the connected-sum map. [F4, F5, step 5.1, step 7.1, step 8.1, construct, algebra]

10.1 The temporary Maslov shift is zero. Reduce this finite chain isomorphism modulo $U$ and compose with the mark-free copy comparison. Its source is the tensor of the two finite hat complexes, so its homology is the tensor of two copies of $\mathbb F_2$, in degree zero. The target also has its single $\widehat{HF}(S^3)$ generator in degree zero by [F5]. Since the induced map is an isomorphism homogeneous of the one common shift, that shift must be zero. This proves the absolute additive Maslov origin, using the actually constructed equivalence rather than assuming it to obtain the inverse. The Alexander origin was already fixed independently by step 7.1. [F1, F5, step 9.1, construct, algebra]

11.1 Localize the polynomial identities at $U$ to obtain the stated $CFK^\infty$ bifiltered equivalence and its inverse homotopies. For the hat conclusion instead specialize those SAME polynomial identities at $U=0$; no flatness assertion about homology is used. The source quotient is literally $C_K\otimes_{\mathbb F_2}C_J$: all generators and differentials are the tensor ones, and step 7.1 gives its sum Alexander filtration. Thus its level $s$ is exactly $\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC_K\otimes F_qC_J$. The maps and homotopies specialize to filtered chain homotopy inverse identities. Apply [F6] to get $\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J)$. This analytic construction uses no grid-identification theorem and makes no claim about a separate grid model. Rank-zero summands use the point-target triangle of [F2], with coefficient one and no added torus; all preceding constructions then reduce to the other factor. Countable choice is used only in the supplied finite-diagram analytic choices and their generic sequence arguments. [F2, F4, F5, F6, step 7.1, step 9.1, step 10.1, construct, algebra] ∎
